headline: In Atlanta basketball, the Southside makes the players and the AUC makes the noise.
summary: Atlanta basketball runs on three circuits. Rec centers and neighborhood courts anchor the Southside and Westside. A deep prep and AAU pipeline stretches from College Park through Gwinnett and Cobb. The AUC carries HBCU pride through Morehouse and Clark Atlanta. Above it all, the Hawks, the WNBA's Dream and the Hawks' G League team in College Park share one metro, and MLK Day is the city's biggest basketball moment.

insights.title: The Southside is the talent engine
insights.detail: College Park, East Point, South Atlanta and Decatur have produced a long line of NBA players, including Dwight Howard, Josh Smith and Derrick Favors. Locals claim them by neighborhood and high school, not by college or draft team.
insights.implication: Tell player stories by zip code and school. Co-brand with neighborhood rec centers and community programs, not only Hawks moments.

insights.title: Hip-hop and hoops are one scene
insights.detail: Atlanta's rap artists, courtside and in the stands, are part of how the Hawks are experienced. Local hoopers treat sneakers and music as a shared language, and artists from the city regularly shape what gets worn on and off court.
insights.implication: Collaborate with Atlanta artists and stylists on drops, with credit and payment. Let the music calendar set release timing as much as the NBA calendar does.

insights.title: HBCU basketball is a cultural anchor
insights.detail: Morehouse and Clark Atlanta play in the Southern Intercollegiate Athletic Conference. With Spelman and the wider Atlanta University Center, they give the city a basketball identity rooted in Black college life. Homecoming season and campus gym culture matter as much as arena nights.
insights.implication: Build HBCU-informed capsules with the schools' licensing offices and student creators. Launch them during homecoming and the winter conference season.

insights.title: Gwinnett and the suburbs carry the prep rivalries
insights.detail: Suburban programs in Gwinnett, Cobb and DeKalb compete in Georgia's big-school classifications. Private programs like Southwest Atlanta Christian and Pace Academy add another tier. High school pride is loud and hyper-local.
insights.implication: Make school-color team and warm-up product tied to named programs, under proper licensing. It would land harder than generic city graphics.

insights.title: Three pro teams, one market
insights.detail: The Hawks play at State Farm Arena. The WNBA's Atlanta Dream are a real second fandom with a strong Black and women-led base, and the College Park Skyhawks give the Southside its own pro team. Many local fans follow all three.
insights.implication: Plan women's and G League stories alongside the Hawks calendar, with Dream-specific product. Don't treat them as afterthoughts.

insights.title: MLK Day is the signature basketball moment
insights.detail: The Hawks have a traditional MLK Day home game, and the 2026-27 one is on Jan 18 against the 76ers. A reported return of the 2020-21 MLK City Edition would tie straight into it.
insights.implication: Make the MLK game the anchor of the season: community programming, a respectful capsule, and stories co-created with King Center-adjacent and local Black-led organizations.

places.name: State Farm Arena
places.why: Home of the Hawks, an occasional Dream venue and the stage for the MLK Day game.

places.name: Gateway Center Arena
places.why: Primary home of the WNBA's Atlanta Dream and the G League College Park Skyhawks, and the anchor of the Southside's pro basketball.

places.name: Hank McCamish Pavilion
places.why: Georgia Tech's home court, and a college hoops rallying point inside the city.

places.name: Forbes Arena at Morehouse College
places.why: Home of Morehouse basketball and a symbol of HBCU hoops pride.

places.name: Clark Atlanta University gymnasium
places.why: Home court for the Panthers and the Morehouse rivalry across the AUC.

places.name: Georgia State Convocation Center
places.why: Home of Georgia State, a downtown college option with a commuter and local-grad fanbase.

places.name: Dunbar Recreation Center
places.why: A long-standing city rec center on the Southside corridor, the kind of gym where neighborhood leagues and pickup shape local hoopers.

places.name: Adamsville Recreation Center
places.why: A Southwest Atlanta city rec site, typical of the Westside and Southside youth leagues.

people.name: Dwight Howard
people.role: NBA champion and former No. 1 pick
people.why: A Southwest Atlanta Christian alum, claimed by the city as its biggest prep-to-pro story.

people.name: Josh Smith
people.role: Former Hawks forward and College Park native
people.why: A homegrown Hawks star of the 2000s, and still a streetball and local-media figure.

people.name: Derrick Favors
people.why: A South Atlanta High product who stands for the city's Southside pipeline.

people.name: Dominique Wilkins
people.role: Hawks Hall of Famer and team ambassador
people.why: The Human Highlight Film is the franchise's defining legend, even though he grew up elsewhere.

people.name: Jalen Johnson
people.why: The current face of the franchise and its All-NBA anchor.

people.name: Atlanta Dream
people.why: The market's second pro fandom, with a loyal base and star players such as Allisha Gray and Rhyne Howard.

people.name: Quin Snyder
people.why: His defense-first system sets the style of Atlanta's current identity.

moments.name: MLK Day Hawks home game
moments.why: Atlanta's traditional MLK Day game is set for 2:30 p.m. ET against the 76ers on NBC/Peacock.

moments.name: Emirates NBA Cup group play
moments.why: The Hawks open at Boston on Oct 30 in East Group C. The Dec 11 final is set for Hinkle Fieldhouse.

moments.name: Specter uniform games
moments.why: The Hawks are one of eight historic franchises getting Nike's Specter uniform, a direct product moment.

moments.name: HBCU homecoming and SIAC season
moments.why: AUC homecoming and the SIAC season put Black college basketball culture in the foreground.

moments.name: Summer pro-am and AAU circuits
moments.why: Metro summer leagues and AAU events put local prospects on display during the NBA offseason.

vocabulary.meaning: Local shorthand for Atlanta, used constantly by natives.
The airport code turned city brand, common on streetwear and tees.
Atlanta as a center of Black culture, business and education.
The regional hip-hop identity that shaped Atlanta's style and swagger.
East Atlanta police-zone shorthand, made famous by Gucci Mane and worn as neighborhood pride.
Dominique Wilkins' nickname, and a reference point for Hawks dunk culture.

designCues.source: The Hawks' volt-green accent from recent franchise identity
designCues.use: A high-visibility accent on warm-ups and footwear, not a dominant field.

designCues.source: The franchise's primary red, which links back to the Hawks' classic uniforms
designCues.use: Pair with black for team-forward product and nostalgic Wilkins-era references.

designCues.source: The state's clay soil, which underlies the metro area's ground
designCues.use: An earthy accent in apparel colorways that gives them a Georgia feel.

designCues.source: Atlanta's Peach State identity and everyday ATL branding
designCues.use: Keep peach motifs and ATL lettering understated and in small details, not clichéd front graphics.

designCues.source: AUC athletic lettering and varsity styles seen across campuses
designCues.use: Draw on varsity block forms for original graphics, and license any school marks through the institutions.

designCues.source: The MLK Day game and the 2020-21 MLK-honoring City Edition
designCues.use: Keep the tone reverent and develop it with Black-led partners. Skip slogans and decorative use of King's likeness or words.

productHooks: MLK Day capsule timed to the Jan 18 game, co-developed with Atlanta Black-led organizations and designers.
Specter-uniform lifestyle and warm-up product in Hawks red, black and volt green.
Southside heritage capsule built on College Park, East Point and South Atlanta school and neighborhood stories.
Dream and Skyhawks co-branded apparel that sits alongside the Hawks lines.
Licensed HBCU basketball warm-ups with Morehouse and Clark Atlanta for homecoming and SIAC season.
watchouts: Don't use MLK's name, image or words as decoration. Work with the King estate and local Black-led partners on any MLK product.
College and high school marks need licenses. Don't imitate school logos without permission.
Avoid trap and rap stereotypes. Credit and pay Atlanta artists, stylists and photographers for any cultural contribution.
Don't name or show high school players beyond public records and the licensing rules for amateur athletes.
